newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, awaits LME July options.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, awaits LME July options.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker in light, lackluster trading ahead of the closely-watched July LME options declarations on Wednesday.
September COMEX copper ended 2.10 cents weaker at 110.05 cents, traded 112.45 to 109.80 cents. Spot July went out 1.50 cents lower at 112.15 cents. Volume was estimated at 8,500 lots.
LME stocks rose a hefty 3,175 tonnes Tuesday to 128,325 tonnes.
Late Monday BHP said that shipments of copper concentrates from its Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea resumed following rains during the weekend.
Shipments were suspended June 2 because there was not enough water in the river for barges to sail.
Striking employees at Inco Ltd in Canada have also returned to work.
"All these factors discouraged the market from going higher," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said. "With a holiday coming up in the U.S., some people also took profits."
The London backwardation remained firm at $120/$130.
Dealers were hoping a more confident, less choppy and higher copper market will emerge once the LME July options declarations pass on Wednesday.
COMEX copper futures trading ends one hour early at 1300 EDT Thursday. The exchange is closed Friday because of Independence Day.
